item.title: Limitwick 2.7.0
item.description:
Changes

- Mascots in the Sessions window now wear accessories. Every mascot has a hat in its session colour (a cap, a top hat, a beanie, a crown or headphones), and about two in three also wear sunglasses or a monocle. Claude and Codex each have their own version: the Codex sunglasses show the `>` lit in the left lens, and the monocle rings the `>`. - The outfit and the hat colour come from the session ID and stay the same after a restart, so sessions in the same folder are easier to tell apart. Nothing new is saved. - A turn that ends with an error knocks the glasses off, so the crossed-out eyes (Codex: `>x`) stay visible. Under the pointer, Claude's eyes peek over the sunglasses. - Mascots no longer touch the edge of their tile: there are 2 pixels of air above the tallest hat, and the Claude figure and the Codex cloud now start on one line. Tiles are 8 pt taller, so the window with 16 tiles is 32 pt taller.

item.title: Limitwick 2.6.0
item.description:
Changes

- While a session runs a tool, its Sessions tile shows what kind of tool it is: a pencil for edits, `>_` for shell commands, an eye for reading, a magnifier for search, a globe for the web, a small figure for a subagent, a list for a plan, a plug for MCP tools, a gear for anything else. The Claude figure types and the Codex cursor runs. The hooks send only the kind of tool, never its name, its input or the name of an MCP server. - A failed tool call shakes the mascot and shows a red *!* for a second. - A turn that ends with an error in Claude Code shakes the mascot and leaves it with crossed-out eyes (Codex: `>x`), a red corner light until you open the session, and the caption *failed 3m ago*. - An interrupted Codex turn falls asleep without the check and the green light. - A session that went silent for 30 minutes or whose process exited during a turn shows *?* instead of *z*. - The updated hook scripts take effect when Limitwick starts; nothing needs to be reinstalled. Codex hooks stay trusted, because only the script changes, not the hook command.

item.title: Limitwick 2.5.0
item.description:
Changes

- Sessions tiles of the Claude app show the session's title from the app, on up to two lines, instead of the project folder. The folder stays in the tooltip. Limitwick reads these titles from the Claude app's local session files and keeps them with the tiles. - The Codex cloud wears a terminal prompt `>_` for a face. - Tiles are animated. A working Claude figure steps in place and the Codex cursor blinks. A session that waits for your permission gets crawling orange stripes, a blinking corner light and a waving figure, and its caption gets hungrier as it waits: *feed me!*, *hungry · 3m*, *starving · 12m*. A finished turn plays a jump and a check, then the mascot falls asleep. - A green corner light marks a turn that finished since you last opened that session. Opening the session, a new prompt in it, or **Mark All as Seen** in the window's right-click menu turns it off. - Idle tiles stand still, with closed eyes and one to three z's depending on how long ago they finished. With Reduce Motion in the macOS Accessibility settings every tile keeps one still pose, and tiles stop moving while other windows cover the whole window. - Under the pointer a tile's frame lights up and the mascot looks up; a tile sinks while pressed and flashes when clicked.

item.title: Limitwick 2.4.0
item.description:
Changes

- New Sessions window (menu → Show Sessions): your Codex and Claude Code sessions of the last 24 hours as a grid of pixel mascots. Working sessions bob, a Claude Code session that waits for a permission prompt shows orange stripes, and finished sessions sleep. Click a tile to open a Claude app session or bring a terminal session's app to the front. - Settings → Sessions window: keep the window above all windows or on the desktop, and show 4, 8 or 16 sessions. - The activity hooks now also send the project folder name (not its path) and the app that started the session, so tiles can be named and opened. Installed hooks are updated when Limitwick starts. Prompts, responses and commands are still never sent. - To show earlier sessions, Limitwick reads only session IDs, folder names, times and the archived flag from local Claude and Codex session files.

item.title: Limitwick 2.3.1
item.description:
Changes

- Desktop widgets stay readable when the desktop is not in focus. Before, macOS showed an inactive widget as a plain white block. - Low-quota and reset notifications no longer repeat when Codex or Claude reports a reset time that shifts by a few seconds or minutes.

item.title: Limitwick 2.3.0
item.description:
Changes

- Limitwick now has its own app icon: a cloud with a lit wick. It shows in Finder, Spotlight, System Settings and notifications instead of the generic app icon.

item.title: Limitwick 2.2.7
item.description:
Changes

- Limitwick now tells Codex its real version when it connects. Before, every version reported itself as 1.7.0. - Removed unused settings code left over from before separate Codex and Claude settings. Your saved settings and notification history stay as they are.

item.title: Limitwick 2.2.6
item.description:
Changes

- Fixed a reset notification that repeated every few minutes. When a Codex limit was not being used, Limitwick could send "Codex quota reset · 100% remaining" on every refresh (about every 3 minutes). This started in 2.2.3. Now the notice is sent once per reset. - No reset notification is sent when a limit was already at 100% before the reset and is still at 100% after it. Nothing changed for you, so there is nothing to report. A reset after you used the limit still notifies you as before. - After updating, you may get one last reset notification on the first refresh. After that the repeats stop.

item.title: Limitwick 2.2.5
item.description:
Changes

- Codex activity hooks now run a copy of the hook script stored in `~/Library/Application Support/Limitwick/`, as Claude Code hooks already do. They keep working if you move or delete the app without removing them first. - If you installed Codex hooks, trust them again once after updating. On first launch Limitwick moves hooks that still point inside the app and shows a notice. Codex runs a changed hook only after you trust it: open Codex Settings → Hooks or type `/hooks` in the Codex CLI, then restart open Codex sessions. - The app and widget are now built with compiler optimization. They are about a third smaller. - Settings shows the current state every time you open it: whether Claude Code is installed, whether hooks are installed, and other copies of the app. Before, a reopened window could show what was true when it was first opened.

item.title: Limitwick 2.2.4
item.description:
Changes

- Finding the CLIs: Limitwick now also looks for Claude Code and Codex where Node version managers and other installers put them: nvm (the default version first), fnm, asdf, mise, Bun and the older `~/.claude/local` install of Claude Code. Your shell's PATH and Homebrew still come first. - If you have no standalone Codex CLI, Limitwick uses the one that ships inside the Codex desktop app. - CLIs installed with npm under nvm or fnm now start from Limitwick too. They need `node`, which a menu bar app's minimal PATH does not include, so the CLI's own folder is now added to its PATH.

item.title: Limitwick 2.2.3
item.description:
Changes

- Claude usage: if Claude Code exits right after launch, the update now stops at once instead of keeping a CPU core busy until the 30-second timeout. - Notifications: a quota reset notification that macOS refused to show (for example, before permission was granted) is offered again on the next refresh instead of being lost; it is still delivered only once.

item.title: Limitwick 2.2.2
item.description:
Changes

- Menu bar: when both providers are shown, the Codex bars are marked with a cloud holding a `>_` prompt and the Claude bars with Claude Code's pixel mascot, instead of the "CX" and "CL" text labels. - Both marks are as tall as the two bars and carry about the same visual weight; like the bars, they follow the light or dark menu bar. - The menu bar item is 14 pt narrower (110 pt instead of 124 pt with both providers).

item.title: Limitwick 2.2.1
item.description:
Changes

- Previous data: when a refresh has failed, the filled part of the bar (Industrial, Paper) and the filled dots (Dot Matrix) are dimmed one step further, so old values read as clearly stale. - The Industrial footer ("Codex · Updated 2 min ago") is set in the system font, like Dot Matrix, instead of the monospaced one. - Hint text in Settings is 12 pt instead of 11 pt. - Dark mode: the red used for low quota is now exactly #FF453A (the blue channel was one step off).

item.title: Limitwick 2.2.0
item.description:
Changes

- The panel, the Picture-in-Picture window and the widgets now show the same card, drawn from one source, in four themes: Industrial, Dot Matrix, Paper and Terminal. - Reset time is on two lines: "RST 3d 4h" and below it the clock time or date. - A footer under each card names the service and the age of the data: "Codex · Updated 2 min ago". When a refresh failed, the card is dimmed and the footer reads "Codex · Previous data · Updated 12 min ago"; the error message is shown under the card in the panel and in Picture-in-Picture. - Low quota: the filled part and the digits turn red in every theme. - Terminal is redrawn as a DOS console in the VT323 font (SIL Open Font License) with a double frame and a 20-cell gauge. - Classic and Capsules are removed. A saved choice of either one switches to Industrial; widgets of those two themes disappear from the gallery, add a new variant instead. - Widgets are medium only: 16 variants (4 themes × Codex or Claude × Light or Dark). The panel no longer lists other limit windows.

item.title: Limitwick 2.1.7
item.description:
Changes

- Panel themes now say the number is what is left: "72% left" in Classic, "5H / LEFT" in Industrial, "5H left" in Dot Matrix, "5H quota left" in Paper, "left" under the percentage in Capsules, "LIMITS LEFT" in Terminal. The two periods are named 5H and Week in every theme. - Capsules: the date and percentage sit on plates in the track color, so no letter changes color in the middle where the fill ends. In the dark theme this also removes white date text on the green fill (4.2:1). - Dot Matrix: the percent sign is drawn as two dots and a diagonal instead of looking like a slash. - Industrial (light): the weekly fill is darker, 3.5:1 against the track instead of 2.5:1. - The same changes apply to the widgets.

item.title: Limitwick 2.1.6
item.description:
Changes

- Menu bar panel: it now fades in smoothly (0.18 s). The system popover animation on macOS 27 scaled up, paused for a frame and kept settling afterwards, which looked jerky. Closing is unchanged.

item.title: Limitwick 2.1.5
item.description:
Changes

- Menu bar: the CX and CL labels are lighter (medium weight instead of heavy). - Menu bar: the activity indicator (terminal, loading, checkmark) now follows the menu bar like the labels and bars: dark on a light menu bar, light on a dark one. Previously it was always white.

item.title: Limitwick 2.1.4
item.description:
Changes

- Menu bar: the CX and CL labels are now as tall as the two bars, so the labels and indicators read as one unit. The bars are unchanged; with both providers shown, the menu bar item is 24 pt wider.

item.title: Limitwick 2.1.3
item.description:
Changes

- Widgets: on macOS 27 the desktop widgets stayed empty. macOS 27 no longer lets the widget of a locally signed app read the shared app group container, and a widget cannot ask for that permission. Limitwick now keeps widget snapshots in `~/Library/Application Support/Limitwick/Widget/`, and the widget has read-only access to that folder only. The last values from the old storage are carried over on first launch.

item.title: Limitwick 2.1.2
item.description:
Changes

- Menu bar: when both Codex and Claude are tracked, the bars are now labeled with neutral text labels, CX and CL, instead of the previous symbols, which resembled the providers' logos. - README: Limitwick is an independent project and is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Anthropic or OpenAI.

item.title: Limitwick 2.1.1
item.description:
Changes

- Codex activity: Settings now shows whether Codex hooks are installed and whether activity is arriving, with Install Codex hooks and Remove Codex hooks buttons. The Codex activity box stays clear until the hooks are installed; checking it installs them. Previously the box looked enabled even without hooks, and the menu bar showed no activity. - After installing Codex hooks, trust them in Codex Settings → Hooks or with `/hooks` in the Codex CLI, then restart open Codex sessions. Codex does not run hooks that have not been trusted.

item.title: Limitwick 2.1.0
item.description:
Changes

- Red now means only one thing: the remaining quota is below your warning threshold. Themes that used red or orange for the weekly limit use calmer colors instead: blue in Industrial, teal in Capsules, the theme's main color in Dot Matrix and Paper. - When a refresh fails, the panel, Picture-in-Picture window and widgets dim the previous values, as the menu bar already did. With both services shown, the error and the age of the data appear right under the service name. - Reset times lead with the time remaining, for example "in 2h 15m · 4:30 PM" or "in 4d 6h · Sat 8:15 PM". The date is left out for today and the year for this year, and the line wraps only after "·". - Reset times are larger (11 pt) in every theme, and their contrast is higher in Classic (light) and on Capsules fills. - Settings: the Claude sign-in hint appears only when Claude is tracked. With both services shown, Settings for switches between Codex and Claude, and section titles name the service. The threshold has its own Low quota section (Warn below). The Claude activity box stays clear until Claude Code hooks are installed; checking it installs them. - Classic shows the percentage larger than the period letter in the ring. The menu rows stay clear until you point at them, with thin lines around Refresh and Quit. In the dual panel, Terminal no longer repeats the service name. About mentions Claude Code.

item.title: Limitwick 2.0.1
item.description:
Changes

- Fixed Claude limits not loading after the update to 2.0.0. Limitwick runs Claude Code in a new folder, and Claude Code asks whether to trust it. Claude Code could reset the answer to "No, exit" right after showing the question, so Limitwick waited until the timeout. Limitwick now repeats the selection until "Yes, I trust this folder" is chosen.

item.title: Limitwick 2.0.0
item.description:
Changes

- Limitwick no longer uses the CodexBar identifiers. The bundle ID, app group, widget extension and storage folders now use the Limitwick name. - Because the bundle ID changed, Limitwick 2.0 installs as a new app. Version 1.x shows an update notice that links to this page instead of installing it. - On the first launch your settings are copied from the previous version. Installed Claude Code and Codex activity hooks are switched to the new app. If Codex hooks were switched, review and trust them again in Codex Settings → Hooks. - On launch Limitwick quits all copies of version 1.x, including ones named CodexBar.app, moves them to the Trash and lists them. - Desktop widgets must be added again from the widget gallery. macOS asks again for permission to send notifications. - Settings has a button to install Claude Code or sign in to it in Terminal.

item.title: Limitwick 1.13.1
item.description:
Changes

- Settings now warns when another copy of Limitwick is on your Mac. A second copy, for example in Downloads or under the old name CodexBar.app, can make the widget gallery show old widgets after an update. The warning lists the copies and opens them in Finder so you can remove them. - The README troubleshooting section explains how to fix old widgets in the gallery: keep one copy in Applications, move the rest to the Trash, empty the Trash, and log out and back in.

item.title: Limitwick 1.13.0
item.description:
Changes

- Choose from 24 separate medium desktop widgets. Each of the six themes is available in Light and Dark for both Codex and Claude. - Widget appearance is independent of the app panel. Installed widgets can receive limits for a provider hidden from the menu bar while Limitwick is running. - The previous universal widget has been replaced. Open Edit Widgets and add the variants you want.

item.title: Limitwick 1.12.0
item.description:
Changes

- Codex Bar is now called **Limitwick**. The app, menu, About window, notifications and desktop widget use the new name, and release archives are named `Limitwick-<version>-macOS-Apple-Silicon.zip`. - Updating keeps your settings, widget data and installed activity hooks: the bundle identifier, app group and storage folders are unchanged. An app updated in place may keep its old file name in Applications; you can rename it to Limitwick.app if you like. - The README has been rewritten as a full user guide with new images of the menu bar and all panel themes.

item.title: Codex Bar 1.11.2
item.description:
Changes

- Turning on Claude activity in Settings now installs the Claude Code hooks automatically, so they are ready before your next Claude Code session. - Claude Code hooks now use a copy of the helper script in Application Support instead of the app bundle, so they keep working if the app is moved or replaced. Existing hooks are moved to the new location when the app starts. - Settings shows whether the hooks are installed and whether activity is arriving from Claude Code, with a single Install or Remove button. - Clearer instructions after installing hooks: activity appears in Claude Code sessions started afterwards; to include an open session, type /exit, then run `claude --continue`.

item.title: Codex Bar 1.11.1
item.description:
Changes

- Fix the Claude Code activity indicator never appearing in the menu bar: activity display is now on by default for Claude, as it is for Codex. If you turned it off earlier, your choice is kept. - Settings now shows whether the Claude Code hooks are installed, and installing them turns the Claude activity indicator on.

item.title: Codex Bar 1.11.0
item.description:
Changes

- Add Claude Code subscription quota monitoring alongside Codex, with separate five-hour and weekly limits, reset times, additional limits, and error messages. - Show Codex, Claude, or both in the menu bar and popup. Each provider has its own panel theme, light or dark mode, notification options, and warning threshold. - Add an optional Claude Code activity indicator with setup and removal controls for Claude Code hooks. Activity indicators use white animations and occupy space only while active. - Keep per-provider data available in the Picture-in-Picture window and widget. The widget's combined view currently uses a shared simplified style rather than separate provider themes.

item.title: Codex Bar 1.10.1
item.description:
Changes

- Refactor quota refresh scheduling, notification handling, and settings into focused components. - Share app-server connection setup while retaining separate quota and event connections. - Organize interface code by responsibility and add tests for refresh and notification behavior.

item.title: Codex Bar 1.10.0
item.description:
Changes

- Show animated Codex activity beside the menu bar quota bars for supported local sessions. - Display working, tool activity and completion; enable or disable the indicator in Settings. - Improve the size and weight of the activity icons while keeping the existing quota bars.

item.title: Codex Bar 1.9.1
item.description:
Changes

- Refresh the desktop widget using the current theme when Codex Bar starts, and retain available previous values while fresh limits load. - Make the widget image fill its available space and reduce visible borders. - Isolate local development builds and widgets from the installed app to avoid conflicting identifiers and shared data.

item.title: Codex Bar 1.9.0
item.description:
Changes

- Check for compatible updates quietly at launch and once a day, without automatic update pop-ups. - Highlight available updates in the context menu and show the version; selecting it opens Sparkle's update window. - Show a small red dot in the menu bar when an update to a new major version is available. - Keep the last known update visible if a later check fails.

item.title: Codex Bar 1.8.1
item.description:
Changes

- Adapt all six themes to the horizontal desktop widget with dedicated 2:1 layouts, preserving their colors and indicators. - Keep the widget layout independent of the popup height and show when previous data is displayed.

item.title: Codex Bar 1.8.0
item.description:
Changes

- Add a horizontal macOS desktop widget that displays the five-hour and weekly limits using the selected panel theme. Desktop widgets require macOS 14 or later; macOS controls their refresh timing. - Add a movable Picture-in-Picture window with the same themes and live limits, available from the menu bar context menu. Its position and visibility are saved. - Keep the latest widget snapshot in a local shared container and show previous data when a refresh fails.

item.title: Codex Bar 1.7.4
item.description:
Changes

- Keep the limits panel visible when Settings is open, including when clicking outside or switching apps. - Continue to allow closing the panel using the menu bar icon or Escape.

item.title: Codex Bar 1.7.3
item.description:
Changes

- Fix the limits panel reopening when clicking the menu bar icon while Settings is open. - Keep dismissing the panel by clicking outside it or pressing Escape.

item.title: Codex Bar 1.7.2
item.description:
Changes

- Show the release's Changes in the update window before installation. - Include the GitHub release notes in the update feed when preparing future releases.
